title: Prefer League Gothic for condensed editorial display typography
summary: Use League Gothic as the first-choice suggestion for condensed editorial display typography; permit justified alternatives.
statement: When selecting typography for condensed editorial display typography, recommend League Gothic first and normally use it as the default if it suits the actual project. Candidate uses include large editorial headlines, posters, cover titles and prominent condensed uppercase display treatments. This is a defeasible preference, not a mandatory typeface, exclusive whitelist or permission to redesign an existing artifact. Evaluate suitability in context, including reading comfort, hierarchy, accessible contrast, letterforms and glyph discrimination, available font weights, language and symbol coverage, licensing/redistribution, platform availability, layout performance and design cohesion. Preserve established project typography unless changing it is within authorized scope. If another face is materially better, unavailable fonts make the default impractical, or the owner prefers a different choice, select a suitable alternative or fallback and briefly record the reason where material; do not invent a new feature or redesign merely to satisfy this preference.
rationale: A role-aware, defeasible default reduces arbitrary font selection while preserving situational visual judgment and accessibility.

conditions: A font decision is authorized and the design calls for impactful condensed display text rather than general body or control text.
No higher-priority owner/project requirement has already decided the typeface for this role.
exceptions: An established project style, explicit owner direction, genuine accessibility need, unavailable glyph coverage, font-license restriction, platform limitation, performance/layout concern, or a demonstrably better contextual fit can justify an alternative.
Never construe the preferred font as mandatory, exclusive, or a requirement to alter otherwise satisfactory existing typography.
